# Draft:Oko kingdom Delta State Nigeria

Oko Kingdom
Oko is a traditional kingdom located in Oshimili South Local Government Area of Delta State, Nigeria. The kingdom sits along the west bank of the River Niger, near Asaba.
Governance
Oko Kingdom operates under a traditional monarchy. The reigning monarch is HRH Osita I, who holds the title of Akor of Oko Kingdom.
Community Structure
Oko Kingdom is composed of six villages grouped into two traditional blocks. The Oseede Block comprises the villages of Amakom, Obiokpu and Anala. The Ekeanya Block comprises the villages of Ogbele, Umuoko and Odifulu.
Economy and Geography
The predominant occupations in Oko Kingdom are fishing and rural agriculture. The area sits along the west bank of the River Niger and is prone to seasonal flooding. In the past, farmers in Oko were forced to travel through neighbouring Anambra State to sell their produce due to poor road conditions.
In March 2026, Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori inaugurated the 4.8-kilometre Oko-Amakom/Oko-Obiokpu/Oko-Anala Road in Oko Kingdom. The road was constructed above the flood level recorded during the 2012 floods. The state government also approved a second phase of the road project valued at 16.9 billion naira, to be completed within 24 months.
